headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Price above a still-falling 200-day average; leverage has cooled

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The market is in an early-stage uptrend with medium confidence (65/100). That supports a measured increase in acquisition spend, weighted toward active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, while holding some budget in reserve: fewer than half of recent days closed above the long-term average, that average is still declining, leveraged traders have become less willing to pay up for long exposure, and long-term interest rates are high. This is a budget-posture view built on past data, not trading advice and not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is 17% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.17).
90-day return of +35%; weekly RSI a firm 60; 50-day average 8% above the 200-day.
Only 48% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average.
200-day average still falling (-5% over 90 days); price 33% below all-time high.
watch: The tension that stands out today is between mood and positioning: Fear & Greed is still at 71 (Greed) and price is up 35% over 90 days, yet the funding z-score has dropped to -0.15 and the sentiment score has roughly halved to +0.21, so leveraged traders are no longer paying up to be long. Underneath that, the trend remains only partly confirmed, with breadth at 48% and the 200-day average still sloping down 5% over 90 days. Funding recovering, breadth moving well above 50% and the 200-day slope turning positive would strengthen the read; price falling back below the 200-day average would weaken it. The 5.26% 10-year yield, and markets being split on a Fed rate rise at the 27 October FOMC meeting, remain the macro backdrop to monitor.
analysis: Short-term sentiment is bullish-leaning (+0.21 of a possible ±1), though only modestly so and noticeably softer than earlier readings: Fear & Greed at 71 (Greed) is what carries the lean, and most of the positioning data sits closer to neutral than that label implies. The clearest thing pulling against the read is funding, where the z-score has slipped to -0.15, meaning leveraged longs are no longer paying an above-normal premium; that fits the CryptoQuant analyst note (Axel Adler Jr., reported by ChainCatcher on 28 September) that futures positioning currently shows buyers with no advantage. The long/short ratio of 1.38 and open interest of about $7.7B still show a mild long tilt, which reinforces the lean without suggesting a crowded trade, and ChainCatcher, citing CoinGlass, put total crypto liquidations at about $241M over the 24 hours to 30 September ($144M longs, $98M shorts), a small, two-sided figure consistent with low leverage stress. Volatility is neither a support nor a threat: realised volatility is at the 50th percentile of its two-year range, Bollinger width is 18%, DVOL is 35.6 and the VIX is 15.9, so both crypto options and equities are pricing calm, while a stablecoin supply ratio of 5.4 indicates a moderate amount of sidelined stablecoin liquidity. As immediate context, Rio Times reported on 30 September that bitcoin closed Tuesday at US$83,622 (+0.14%) after weak US job-openings and consumer-confidence data cut market-implied odds of an October Fed rate rise to about 51.5% from 70.9%. The lean would strengthen if funding turned back positive alongside the greed reading, and would slip to neutral if Fear & Greed cooled while funding stayed flat or negative.

Medium-term momentum is bullish-leaning (+0.39 of a possible ±1), the strongest of the three dimensions. Reinforcing that, the 90-day rate of change is +35%, weekly RSI is 59.8 (firm, but well short of the overbought zone), and the 50-day average sits 8.4% above the 200-day, so the moving-average structure is on the golden-cross side. The main thing cutting against the lean is participation: only 47.8% of the last 90 days closed above the 200-day average, which means the headline gain comes from a relatively recent move rather than a long, consistent run of strength. Network and market-share data are mildly supportive rather than decisive, with active addresses 5% above their yearly average and BTC dominance at 58.3%, showing activity concentrated in bitcoin rather than rotating broadly into altcoins. Flows reinforce the lean: The Block reported on 26 September that US spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $2.4B in the week ending 25 September, their largest week since October 2025 and enough to turn 2026 year-to-date flows positive, although the daily figures shrank each day of that week; Rio Times, citing SoSoValue, reported about US$31M on Monday 28 September, an eighth straight session of net inflows, and the pipeline's latest daily reading is about +$66M. The next scheduled FOMC meeting is 27 October 2026, the main scheduled macro date inside this window, with markets currently split roughly evenly on a rate rise. The lean would strengthen if breadth moved clearly above 50% while ETF inflows held, and would weaken if weekly RSI rolled over or the daily flow streak turned negative.

The long-term trend is bullish-leaning (+0.23 of a possible ±1), but it is an early and not yet fully confirmed lean. What supports it is that price is 17% above its 200-day average (Mayer Multiple 1.17); what cuts against it is that the average itself is still falling, down 5.1% over 90 days. Price has reclaimed the trend line before the trend line has turned up, which is an early-recovery configuration rather than a mature uptrend, and that is why the score is only modestly positive. Valuation neither reinforces nor undermines the lean: the 200-week multiple of 1.26 is mid-range, price is still 33.3% below its all-time high, the Puell Multiple of 1.28 puts miner revenue in a normal band, and the Pi-Cycle gap of -55% is far from the zone that has historically accompanied cycle tops (context only, not scored). Macro is the clearest cross-current: the US 10-year yield is 5.26% against a fed funds rate of 3.63%, so long-dated government debt offers a meaningful competing return to risk assets. Structural demand reinforces the lean, with cumulative spot ETF net inflows of about $57.7B and public companies holding roughly 1.28M BTC; The Block noted on 26 September that year-to-date ETF flows have recovered from roughly -$5.8B in mid-July to positive. The lean would strengthen if the 200-day slope turned positive, and would flip toward neutral or bearish if price fell back below that average while long yields stayed this high.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into non-stablecoin and active-trader channels: the +35% 90-day move, Fear & Greed at 71 and the largest weekly spot ETF inflow since October 2025 (about $2.4B, per The Block) give campaigns a credible, sourced recovery story. With breadth at only 48%, funding now flat (z-score -0.15) and conviction at medium (65/100), lead with trend, institutional participation and product value rather than FOMO urgency, and avoid 'confirmed bull market' claims. Keep stablecoin-first channels defended and some spend flexible while rate expectations around the 27 October FOMC meeting remain unsettled.
